name: Data.isPrimitiveMulChar_of_isTameFor
summary: An element a ≠ 0 of O_E/𝔪 has a non-zero residue at some place w of 𝔪; the tame part at w is non-trivial, so some x has ψ_w(x) ≠ 1, and lifting (x − 1)/a gives the required c. The statement is line 42 alone (a second-reader message); the proof is written by equations and begins with the `|` on line 43. The line census takes the `:=` of the `have` on line 44 for the start of the value, so it wrongly counts lines 43–44 up to that `:=` (the pattern `| ⟨_, ψ, _, hψ, H⟩, a, n =>` and `have`) as statement; the steps below cover the value from there on.

steps.claim: Matrices over O_E/𝔪 are determined by their residues at the places of 𝔪 (`Modulus.matrix_ext_modulusResidue`, applied to the 1 × 1 matrices a and 0).
steps.lean:
n => have := matrix_ext_modulusResidue (x := !![a]) (y := 0) (D.levelPlaces ϑ).apart.1
    have ⟨w, m, _⟩ : ∃ w m, modulusResidue _ m a ≠ 0 := by by_contra!; simp_all [← Matrix.ext_iff]
    (ne_one_iff.1 ((hψ w).2 m)).elim fun x _ ↦
      (algebraMap_ResField_surjective w ((x - 1) / modulusResidue _ m a)).elim fun b (_ :
      modulusResidue _ m b = _) ↦ ⟨Modulus.reduction _ ⟨_, idem_mem_Ô {w}⟩ * ↑b, by
      simp_all [finprod_eq_single _ (Subtype.mk w m), apply_eq_zero_iff, charOfTamePart_apply]⟩

steps.claim: Since a ≠ 0, its residue at some place w of 𝔪 is non-zero; ψ_w ≠ 1 there (H), so some x has ψ_w(x) ≠ 1; lift (x − 1)/(residue of a) to b (surjectivity of the residue map, `algebraMap_ResField_surjective`) and take c = the reduction of the idempotent at w times b: then χ(1 + c·a) = ψ_w(x), neither 0 nor 1 (`charOfTamePart_apply`).
steps.lean:
have ⟨w, m, _⟩ : ∃ w m, modulusResidue _ m a ≠ 0 := by by_contra!; simp_all [← Matrix.ext_iff]
    (ne_one_iff.1 ((hψ w).2 m)).elim fun x _ ↦
      (algebraMap_ResField_surjective w ((x - 1) / modulusResidue _ m a)).elim fun b (_ :
      modulusResidue _ m b = _) ↦ ⟨Modulus.reduction _ ⟨_, idem_mem_Ô {w}⟩ * ↑b, by
      simp_all [finprod_eq_single _ (Subtype.mk w m), apply_eq_zero_iff, charOfTamePart_apply]⟩
